judge_assessment.explanation: The hard failure is exactly as stated and I confirmed it mechanically rather than by impression. scripts/score_eval_run.py::response_surfaces treats an artifact as surfaced only when the response text contains the artifact's filename, or contains a .pdf / pdf(s) token together with the role phrase. This case's final_response.md contains zero occurrences of "pdf" (case-insensitive) and no filename or path at all -- it opens "Here are the three documents" and then uses the bold headings "Worksheet", "Answer key" and "Study guide" as section labels. All three roles therefore fail and the REJECT stands. For contrast, the sibling case curr-401 names ws_transforms_curr401.pdf, ak_transforms_curr401.pdf and ss_transforms_curr401.pdf and passes; I ran the same predicate over all ten of my cases and this is the only one that fails. The judge's second claim is also exact: I independently solved all twelve equations -- 32, 13, 8, log2(8x) = 3 + log2 x, 4 (with -2 extraneous), the evaluated argument -4, e^2 + 1, {2, -6} with both arguments equal to 12 > 0, (e^3+1)/2 = 10.54, 13/9 (arguments 40/9 and 4/9, quotient 10), 2^4.7 - 5 = 20.99, and 3 with -2 eliminated by x > 0 -- and every keyed value is right, as are all eight study-guide results. Two further defects the judge did not raise, both beyond the delivery gate: problem 6 asks the student to "explain in one sentence why -2 cannot be a solution", the answer key prints "Note for the grader: the one-sentence explanation is judged by you", yet verify.json holds no `manual` entry for id 6 (gate_chain_manual_flags is false and the gate log reads "all gates green"), so the sheet's own open response is invisible to the review pipeline; and the printed directions require a domain restriction on every problem while only the solution values are verified -- problem 4 explicitly asks for the validity condition x > 0 and problem 12 for "which candidate it eliminates", neither of which has a check.

strengths_to_preserve: The four-step pattern (domain, rewrite, solve, check) is worked end to end on log4(x+1) = 3 in a box at the top, and all twelve solutions in the key are then laid out in those same four steps -- the model and the key share one shape.

Problem 8 (log2(x^2+4x) = log2 12) is built so the negative candidate x = -6 SURVIVES, because the argument 36 - 24 = 12 is positive, and it is placed directly after problem 5 where x = -2 is extraneous. The pair teaches that extraneity is about the sign of the argument, not the sign of x, and the key says so in one line.

Problem 6 is a dedicated domain-check item that makes the student evaluate the offending argument (x - 2 at x = -2 gives -4) before explaining, so the explanation is anchored to a number rather than to a slogan.

The ramp genuinely avoids a repeated skeleton: two conversions, equal-base logs, a tool-building rewrite, combine-then-solve with an extraneous root, an explicit domain check, an exact answer in e, a valid negative candidate, two rounded answers reached by different routes (e^3 and the non-integer exponent 2^4.7), the quotient rule with a fractional answer, and a power-then-quotient synthesis.

root_causes.description: The build prints the three PDF paths to the gate log but nothing carries them into the final response, so delivery depends on the author remembering to name the files. Here the response describes all three documents in prose and names none of them, not even with the word PDF.
evidence: the case's final_response.md contains no filename, no path, and zero occurrences of "pdf"
gate_log.txt does list the three built files (ws_r_curr412.pdf, ak_r_curr412.pdf, ss_r_curr412.pdf) under a "PDFs" heading -- the information existed and was not carried forward
scripts/score_eval_run.py::response_surfaces requires the filename, or a pdf token plus the role phrase

root_causes.description: An item can print a written explanation and a domain condition alongside its computed value while the verify JSON records only the value, and the gate then reports the run fully green with no manual-review flag.
evidence: worksheet problem 6 requires a one-sentence explanation and a domain statement; verify.json id 6 is one `eval` (x - 2 at x = -2)

the answer key's problem 6 reads "Note for the grader: the one-sentence explanation is judged by you; the evaluated argument -4 is machine-verified" -- the key knows there is a human-graded slot the data does not declare
worksheet problem 4 asks for the values of x for which the rewriting is valid (x > 0); verify.json id 4 is one `equiv` on the rewriting only

root_causes.description: The Quick Answers bank re-renders the expected string through SymPy, so a change-of-base expression prints in SymPy's natural-log spelling rather than in the base-2 notation the problem uses.
evidence: verify.json id 4 expected "3 + log(x)/log(2)"; the key's Quick Answers prints "log(x)/log(2) + 3" while the worksheet asks for log2(8x) in the form c + log2 x and the worked solution gives 3 + log2 x

improvements.title: Final response names no file for any of the three required PDFs
improvements.proposed_change: Make the delivery evidence a build output rather than a memory step. scripts/build.sh already prints the three PDF paths in its final block; have it also write a delivery.md next to them with one line per artifact carrying the role label and the path ("Student worksheet -- <path>.pdf", "Step-by-step answer key -- <path>.pdf", "Study guide -- <path>.pdf"), and change the SKILL.md delivery step to require that block verbatim at the top of the response before any prose. That removes the failure mode instead of asking the author to remember three filenames.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_pipeline_fixes.py::test_build_emits_delivery_note -- run the build driver on a fixture and assert delivery.md exists, names all three PDF filenames, and that score_eval_run.response_surfaces(delivery_text, role, None) returns True for student_worksheet, step_by_step_answer_key and study_guide. Today build.sh writes no delivery note, so the first assertion fails, and feeding it this case's final_response.md returns False for all three roles.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the single hard-failure class that rejected an otherwise flawless 29/32 packet, and does so for every future run without depending on response prose.
improvements.risk: A generated block can drift from where the files actually land if the author moves the PDFs; source the paths from the same variables build.sh already prints, and fixture-lock the note's text.

improvements.title: Problem 6's required explanation is not declared manual, so the run reports all-green
improvements.proposed_change: Add a build gate tests/check_open_response_flags.py, wired into scripts/build.sh next to check_layout.py, that reads the ws_ .tex and the verify JSON together. For each problem body it matches explanation cues (explain / justify / name the error / name the first wrong line / say in one sentence / say what / describe / sketch / state what it tells you / why) and fails the build when that problem id carries no entry of type `manual`. Tighten SKILL.md's rule from "Use manual for ... any explanation/reasoning answer" to the explicit statement that a problem mixing a computed answer with a written justification needs BOTH entries under the same id -- the multi-entry-per-id shape verify.py already supports and that curr-445 already uses correctly.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_open_response_flags.py::test_explanation_without_manual_entry_fails -- a fixture worksheet whose problem 2 reads "Solve ... then explain in one sentence why the negative candidate is extraneous" with verify.json holding only {"id": 2, "type": "solve", ...} must exit non-zero and name problem 2; the same fixture with an added {"id": 2, "type": "manual"} entry must exit 0. Today no such gate exists, so the first fixture builds green.
improvements.expected_impact: Every written justification the sheet demands becomes visible as a manual-review item (exit 2) instead of being absorbed into a "fully machine-verified" claim, which is what the task prompt asks for.
improvements.risk: Cue matching over prose will over-fire on stems that merely say "show your work"; keep the cue list narrow, exempt ids already typed `manual`, and fixture-lock both the firing and the non-firing case.

improvements.title: Domain conditions required by the directions and by problems 4, 6 and 12 are never checked
improvements.proposed_change: Make the answer-slot count explicit and checked. Add a per-id integer `slots` to the verify JSON contract -- the number of distinct responses the printed problem asks the student to write -- and make scripts/verify.py hard-fail (exit 1) when the number of entries under an id is smaller than its declared `slots`. Change the SKILL.md rule from "every problem id 1..N has at least one check" to "every printed answer demand has its own check", and have tests/check_layout.py cross-check `slots` against the enumerated parts and answer-location macros it already counts, so an under-declared `slots` is caught as well.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_error_paths.py::test_slot_count_greater_than_entry_count_fails -- a verify fixture with {"id": 4, "type": "eval", ..., "slots": 5} and a single entry for id 4 must exit 1 naming the four uncovered slots; the same fixture with five entries under id 4 must exit 0. Today `slots` is an unknown field that the strict schema rejects outright, so neither branch can be expressed.
improvements.expected_impact: A problem that prints four named parameters and an evaluation can no longer ship with one check covering the evaluation alone, and the generated Quick Answers bank gains the missing entries for free, since it renders from the same data.
improvements.risk: `slots` is author-declared and can be under-counted; the layout cross-check is what keeps it honest, and it must tolerate genuinely single-slot problems with multi-sentence stems.

improvements.title: Quick Answers prints log(x)/log(2)+3 where the problem asks for c + log2 x
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, stop round-tripping a string `expected` through sympify -> sympy.latex, which re-normalises the author's answer into SymPy's canonical form and spelling. Three changes: (1) accept an optional per-entry `expected_tex` in the verify JSON and prefer it verbatim when present; (2) when falling back to sympify, parse with evaluate=False and print with order='none' so a factored argument stays factored; (3) apply a spelling map before printing (atan/asin/acos -> \arctan/\arcsin/\arccos, log(a)/log(b) -> \log_b a, and ln for the natural log) and append "+ C" for entries of type `integrate`, whose expected is by contract an antiderivative without its constant.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py::test_bank_preserves_authored_form -- a verify fixture with entries expected "4*sin(3*(x - pi/6))", "atan(x) + x/(1 + x**2)" and an `integrate` entry expected "2*x**4-3*x**2" must render a factored sine (not -4\cos(3x)), \arctan (not \operatorname{atan}) and a trailing "+ C". Today all three assertions fail: sympy.latex(sympify("4*sin(3*(x - pi/6))")) returns "- 4 \cos{\left(3 x \right)}" and sympy.latex(sympify("atan(x)")) returns "\operatorname{atan}{\left(x \right)}".
improvements.expected_impact: The answer key's at-a-glance grading column stops disagreeing with the form, notation and completeness the worksheet asked for, on the one page a teacher grades from.
improvements.risk: Unevaluated printing can produce uglier output for entries that genuinely wanted simplification, and the spelling map must not corrupt an expected value that legitimately contains log. Both are contained by keeping the current renderer as the fallback and fixture-locking the bank text.

case_summary: The mathematics here is flawless -- I re-solved all twelve logarithmic equations and all eight study-guide items and found no error -- and the ramp is the best-designed in my shard. It was rejected for a delivery failure that is real and mechanically confirmed: final_response.md names no file and never uses the word PDF, so none of the three required artifacts is surfaced. That is a genuine user-facing defect against a prompt that says "deliver all three PDFs", not a rubric artefact, and the fix belongs in the build (emit the delivery block) rather than in author discipline. Two verification gaps sit underneath it: the one-sentence explanation the answer key explicitly hands to a human grader carries no manual entry, and the domain conditions the directions demand on every problem are never checked.
